t: You're at the Temple Church, between Fleet Street and the Thames, a round church built by the Knights Templar as their English headquarters. It was consecrated in 1185. In King John's reign it served as the royal treasury. It's famous for its round shape and its 13th and 14th century stone effigies. German bombing in the Second World War badly damaged it, and it has been restored and rebuilt since. Buried here are William Marshal, who served five kings, and his son, the second Earl of Pembroke. Bertrand de Blanchefort, a Templar Grand Master, is buried here too. So is the writer Oliver Goldsmith.
